cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this week's review the book holds five calls: the S&P 500 put against widening credit, long US energy stocks, long the yen, long US natural gas and short wheat through the fund. Three reasons are fully in place and two are weakened. The put is the book's biggest gain, up about 81% on its premium after the index fell 1.8% on Friday to 7,580, 2.3% under the entry close, with credit still wider than before the move began and eight sessions to the planned close; the Friday fall came from technology earnings rather than from credit, so it is on the path the note drew but not for the note's reason. Wheat closes on Wednesday at about 16% on the short, with funds now building a short of their own rather than buying back. Energy stocks are 7% above entry with oil at $104, but the daily check tripped the call on Friday because the bond-yield half of the setup has handed back 44% of its rise, so it is weakened and held. Natural gas is weakened for a third week and we now say trim by half: the oil-to-gas gap narrowed on paper, but the fund fell another 5% as it rolled into a dearer December contract, November is forecast to be among the mildest on record, and we no longer expect the call to finish positive even with the base rate. The yen call gave back last week's move, with dollar-yen at 157.80 after the Bank of Japan held, and Tokyo repeated on Monday that it stands ready to act. A reader holding the calls trims gas by half and changes nothing else; the things to watch this week are whether the S&P 500 holds under 7,818, whether wheat's planned close on Wednesday lands near 600, and whether gas prints a weekly close below 2.45.

book.basis: equal weight across the open calls, one unit each, trailing 63 sessions; a 21-session driftless range

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: the fund's loss to Friday's close (about -10.7%) plus the base-rate catch-up scaled to the six weeks left (about +3.6% of the +7.6% three-month median, since the ratio is still above the 95th percentile), less about a point for the fund's cost of rolling contracts in a market where later months trade higher; lowered from last week's -2
calls.view_now: The reason for the call is still there: oil is at $104 and gas at 2.90, the gap between them sits at the 97th percentile of readings since 2000, and funds hold the largest short in the record and are still adding to it. But the gap has not closed the way the note said for seven weeks, and the fund lost another 5% this week to the contract roll alone, so it is about 11% under entry with six weeks to the planned close. A cold turn in the forecast would move gas sharply with that short as fuel, which is why we do not call the thesis broken; but with storage above average and November forecast mild, we now expect the call to finish well under water, with about a one-in-four chance of getting back to even.
calls.action_reason: Reduce by half. The reason for the call is in place but the vehicle is bleeding: the fund paid up to roll contracts again this week and will do so monthly, so a flat gas price loses money, and our expected finish is now about -8% against the +7.6% called for. Half stays on because the record fund short and the extreme gap can reverse on one cold forecast, and the exit level, a weekly close below 2.45, is about 15% away. The review closes the rest if the ratio falls back under the 95th percentile or funds start buying back their short while gas keeps falling.
calls.weakened_reason: Every condition still holds, but the fund the reader owns fell another 5% to 9.08, about 11% under entry, in a week when the quoted front-month price rose only because the November contract expired and the dearer December contract took its place; the fund paid that difference when it rolled. Storage is now about 1% above the five-year average after an 80 billion cubic foot addition in the week to Oct 23, November is forecast to be among the mildest on record, and with six weeks left we no longer expect the call to finish positive even with the note's base rate added in.

calls.title: Yields and oil are surging together. Energy stocks gained after that in 7 of 8 cases.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the average fund return over six months in the eight earlier cases, with the 10% weekly-close exit applied
calls.expected_basis: the gain to Friday's close (about +7.3%) plus a smaller remaining path than the note's average: the two cases closest to today, with oil above $90, returned +8.7% and +4.6%, and the yield half of the setup has reversed, so we take about +8% rather than the +10.1% the eight-case average gave; lowered from last week's 10
calls.view_now: The oil half of the setup is stronger than when the call was made, with US crude at $104 and the energy fund 7% above entry and 19% above its 200-day average, while the broad market fell. The yield half has gone the other way: the 10-year yield has given back 44% of the rise the note was built on and the daily check flagged it on Friday, though at 4.94% it is still 19 basis points above the line that would undo the call. We still expect the call to finish ahead, carried by oil, but a little under what the note called for, because the two earlier cases with oil above $90 made less than the average and the yield leg no longer helps.
calls.action_reason: The critical reason for the call, expensive oil, is more in place than at publication and the fund is ahead, so the call is held; the exit level at 58.72 is 16% below the market. The review will close it if US crude falls out of the top fifth of its three-year range, and will weigh a close if the 10-year yield prints below 4.75%, which the note made the line for the yield half.
calls.weakened_reason: Every written condition still holds, but the daily check tripped the call on Oct 30: the setup was yields and oil surging together, and the yield half has reversed, giving back 44% of its rise (5.24% on Oct 9 to 4.94% on Oct 30) against the one-third limit the note set. Oil, the critical condition, is stronger than at publication at $104.12, and the fund is about 7% above entry, so the trip does not reach the thesis, but it removes half of what made the eight earlier cases alike.

calls.title: The last buyers just showed up in wheat
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate between its one-month (-5.3%) and three-month (-6.6%) medians for a two-month horizon, taken as a short return
calls.expected_basis: the gain to Friday's close (about +16.2% on the short) less a little give-back over the four sessions left, with no further drift added because the fund selling the note relied on is finished and funds are now short themselves
calls.view_now: Wheat fell a ninth straight week, from 625 to 603.5, after Russia let grain ships leave its Azov Sea ports for the first time since July, and the fund the reader shorts closed Friday at 22.20, about 16% below entry. Funds have gone from a record long to a growing short and have not begun buying back, so the squeeze that would end the move has not started, though with funds now short rather than long the edge the note bought is spent. Four sessions remain to the planned close on Wednesday; we expect the call to finish close to where it is, more than double what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: Nothing in the reason for the call has changed and the planned close is Wednesday, Nov 4, when the scorer closes it; there is no case for acting ahead of that with the exit level 27% away. Because funds are now short rather than long, the note is not re-opened or extended at the planned close.

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the note's months-two-to-six median move applied from Friday's 157.80 (about +7% on dollar-yen to 147), with nothing yet earned on the fund, cut by about two and a half points because the record rests on three episodes and the move has not started with eleven weeks left; back to the 4.5 of two weeks ago from last week's 5
calls.view_now: Last week's move did not hold: dollar-yen closed Friday at 157.80, back where the call started, after the Bank of Japan left its rate at 1.25% and traders read it as less hawkish, even though a December rise is about 80% priced. Tokyo has not stepped back; the finance minister repeated on Monday that the joint statement with the United States stands and that the government is ready to act. The fund is flat against entry with eleven weeks to run, and speculators have added to their long yen position, now at the 84th percentile of three years, which means part of the move is already positioned for. We still expect the call to pan out, but we take back last week's small raise because the start we thought we saw has been reversed.
calls.action_reason: The reason for the call, an official campaign the authorities keep standing behind, is intact and was restated on Monday, and the fund is flat with the exit level 3.9% away. The review closes it if the authorities step back from the joint statement or if dollar-yen prints a weekly close above 164.

calls.title: Credit spreads widening, S&P 500 likely to close the gap
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return on the put, restated on Oct 29 when the Scorecard was corrected to mark the SPY 773 put the note told the reader to buy instead of the index: the put's modelled value if the S&P 500 falls the median 3.2% of the five cases (to about 7,510) by the planned close on Nov 11, about 24.5 a share against the 11.71 premium. Last week's review graded the same call on the index, at 3.2%; that figure stays on the record and this one replaces it because the row is now marked on the put
calls.expected_basis: the five cases' finishes fifteen sessions after the signal, re-priced on the put from Friday's level: the median case (index down 3.2%) is worth about 111% on the premium and the average of the five about 130%, but two of the five finished within half a per cent of flat, which on the put means losing 80 to 90% of the premium; weighting those in, and the roughly 4 a share of time value that decays if the index stalls, we put the expected finish at about 100%, in a range from about -85% to about +440%
calls.view_now: Both conditions hold: credit is still 59 basis points wider than when the move began, and the S&P 500 has not come near its record. The index fell 1.8% on Friday to 7,580 after weak results and guidance from Intel, Amazon and Alphabet, which puts it 2.3% under the entry close after eight of the sixteen sessions, on the path of the five earlier cases, whose median finish was a 3.2% fall. The put the note told the reader to buy is worth about 21.25 a share against the 11.71 paid, a gain of about 81%, with eight sessions to the planned close and the exit level 3.1% away. We still expect the call to finish about where the note said, but the range is wide: two of the five cases ended almost flat, which on a put means losing most of the premium.
calls.action_reason: The reason for the call is still there and the index is moving the way the five cases did, so the call runs to its planned close on Nov 11 or the exit level. The gain is already about 81% of the premium; a reader who wants to bank part of it is taking the time value off the table, not changing the view. The review closes it only if the high-yield spread falls back below 300 basis points.
